questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some pants are shirts.

No shirt is a tie.

**Conclusions:**

I. All pants can never be ties.

II. All ties are pants.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bec0009a71dd4faa810855708a98acc31ccc271eb1cbab6220c04442a4b0b1bf.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All pants can never be ties → Follows (because only some pants are shirts and no shirt is a tie, hence all pants can never be ties.)

II. All ties are pants → Does not follow (because only some pants are shirts and no shirt is a tie, hence all ties can never be pants.)

Hence, “Only conclusion I follows”.

questions.question:
Which two numbers (not the digits of the numbers), from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

42 ÷ 2 + 13 − 5 × 7 = 9
questions.solution:
__BODMAS RULE:__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/337cba09b098a129c60c88ca431dc00f7470bb1b39c1452e8d81688a7d6b6b0e.png] 

Let's check each option:

1. 2 and 7

Given equation: 42 ÷ 2 + 13 − 5 × 7 = 9

After interchanging the signs, we get:

⇒__**42 ÷ 7**__ + 13 − 5 × 2 = 9 

⇒6 + 13 − __**5 × 2**__ = 9 

⇒__**6 + 13**__ - 10 = 9
